title: Atol CD's Maarch Courrier hook must be coordinated with XeniT because AmeXio owns both leads
content:
The mechanism is a Maarch Courrier or Alfresco hook dispatching a typed operation on mail-flow approval. Mail flow is the useful specialisation here: incoming correspondence in a French public body is routed, assigned and signed off, and the approval is the event the process exists to produce.

The actionable content is ownership. AmeXio Group owns Atol CD and also XeniT, which carries the seven-lead Alfresco demo, so two entries that look like independent leads are one account. The recorded instruction is to coordinate as one group conversation. Approaching them separately risks two uncoordinated pitches into the same organisation, with the second one arriving as a surprise.

The single lead recorded here is Atol CD, based in Dijon with five further sites, marked "2 · next"; XeniT sits in the Alfresco cohort at "2 · next" as well. Their shared Alfresco surface means one integration plausibly serves both, which strengthens the case for a single conversation rather than merely tidying it.
